question.problem:
$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2(x+2y)}{3}, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1+4y}{3}, & 0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Let $X$ and $Y$  be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $Y$ are shown above. Find the conditional variance $\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=1]$ given that the corresponding expected value is ${\mu }_{X|1}=\frac{8}{15}.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] & =\text{E}[(X-{\mu }_{X|y})^{2}\,|\,Y=y] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where 

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Note that $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]$ is a function of $y.$ 

The conditional density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ can be computed as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{2(x+2y)}{3})}{(\frac{1+4y}{3})} \\  & =\frac{2(x+2y)}{1+4y},\end{aligned}
$$

 

where $0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1.$ Outside this domain, we have ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=0.$ 

Now, substituting $y=1$ into the expression for ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y),$ we get

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)=\frac{2(x+2\cdot 1)}{1+4\cdot 1}=\frac{2x+4}{5}.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=1] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}(\frac{2x+4}{5})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{[\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}+\frac{4{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{4}{3})-0] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\frac{11}{6}] \\  & =\frac{11}{30}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=1] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=1]-{\mu }_{X|1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{11}{30}-{(\frac{8}{15})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{37}{450}.\end{aligned}
$$
